name: NutriRoute Cart Vendor All-Season Stand Kit
description:
The full working uniform of a NutriRoute licensed street cart vendor — one of the Circuit tier's most visible workers, stationed at transit hubs, factory gates, and corridor intersections through all weather. The foundation is a pair of straight-cut black synth-cotton trousers with deep side pockets and a reinforced inner-thigh panel for long hours of standing and squatting. The primary layer is a NutriRoute branded quarter-zip pullover in safety orange with a white NutriRoute wordmark across the chest and a QR patch on the left sleeve that links to the cart's live menu — updated remotely by the vendor. The quarter-zip collar can be pulled high against wind; the cuffs are tight-knit to keep out cold without hampering hand movement. Over it in cold weather: a padded gilet in charcoal with a high mock-neck collar, multiple zippered chest pockets for holding Quanta-chip payment terminals, and hi-vis silver strips at the shoulder seams.

On the head: a NutriRoute-branded mesh-back cap in orange and black, the brim curved and worn low against sun or drizzle. A full-length black synthetic-rubber apron ties at the waist and chest, covering the front of the outfit during service — stain-resistant, wipe-clean, with a front kangaroo pocket holding order-slip printouts and a pen-stylus. Footwear is a pair of Foundry Broadfoot Work Sneakers in black — cushioned for standing shifts, oil-resistant sole, slightly scuffed from daily use. The vendor's hands are bare for service speed, knuckles often chapped from cold. A small bioluminescent flower sticker — personal, not corporate — is stuck to the inside brim of the cap, glowing faintly blue: the only soft thing in the whole outfit.
functionality: QR-linked menu sleeve patch, Quanta-chip terminal pockets in gilet, stain-resistant wipe-clean apron with order-slip pocket, high collar wind protection, oil-resistant cushioned work sneakers, deep cargo pockets, high-visibility shoulder strips
what_it_says: A licensed NutriRoute vendor — not a gray-market operator, an actual franchisee who paid the licensing fee and wears the logo. That costs something, and it buys a certain legitimacy: transit authority doesn't hassle you, the corporate protection window means you're not paying protection to anyone else either. The bioluminescent sticker under the cap brim is the tell that there's a whole person inside the uniform — someone who likes small beautiful things and keeps one hidden on their person at all times.
worn_by: street food operators at transit hubs
manufacturer: NutriRoute corponation (branded pullover, cap, apron); Foundry (sneakers); charcoal gilet from circuit market independent label
price_range: Φ 120–Φ 175 (franchise kit partially subsidized by NutriRoute licensing agreement)
story_hooks: The QR sleeve patch on a vendor's pullover links to the live menu — but a secondary layer beneath the public-facing QR quietly logs the BCI signatures of every person who scans it, feeding data to an unknown third party.

A NutriRoute vendor at a specific factory gate has been working the same corner for eleven years and knows every face, every schedule, every vehicle that passes — they are the best possible witness to whatever happened the night the shift supervisor disappeared.

The bioluminescent sticker inside the cap brim is not a decoration: it's a marker, a signal to someone who knows what to look for, indicating that this vendor is a message drop point for a Circuit-level mutual aid network.

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian street vendor silhouette—compact, functional, weather-sealed. The safety orange pullover and cap create high visibility at transit hubs; the charcoal gilet adds layered warmth without bulk. The black apron dominates the front, creating a stark contrast that reads as 'working class infrastructure.' Overall impression: reliable, visible, built for 12-hour shifts in all conditions.
physical_description.fit: Straight-cut and deliberately roomy through the torso for movement and layering; quarter-zip pullover sits at natural waist; gilet drapes loosely over it without constraining. Trousers are relaxed-straight with reinforced thighs—designed for squatting and standing, not style. Apron hangs full-length from chest to mid-shin, creating an austere vertical line.
physical_description.primary_material: NutriRoute pullover: synth-cotton blend (durable, temperature-regulating). Trousers: black synth-cotton with reinforced panels. Gilet: padded synthetic insulation with ballistic nylon shell. Apron: full synthetic rubber (food-service grade, wipeable). Sneakers: vulcanized synthetic leather and mesh, oil-resistant sole.
physical_description.texture: Pullover is soft-knit with a slight sheen; cuffs are tightly ribbed. Gilet is quilted with a matte nylon exterior and a subtle grip texture at the shoulders (from repeated handling of cart equipment). Apron is smooth and slightly tacky—designed to resist stains. Sneakers show scuffing at the toe box and heel; sole is textured for wet-surface grip.
physical_description.color_scheme: Safety orange (NutriRoute branding) as dominant accent; black as primary (trousers, cap bill, apron, sneakers). Charcoal gilet provides neutral mid-tone. White wordmark on chest. Hi-vis silver strips at gilet shoulders. Contrast is high and intentional—visibility is a job requirement.
physical_description.closures: Quarter-zip neck on pullover (friction-fit at cuffs). Gilet secured with center zip and two horizontal chest zips for quick terminal access. Apron ties at waist and chest with synthetic cord. Sneakers use standard laces with slight wear at the eyelets.
distinctive_features: QR code patch on left pullover sleeve—linked to live cart menu, updated remotely by vendor
NutriRoute wordmark in white across chest—corporate branding, instantly identifiable
Multiple zippered chest pockets on gilet—designed to hold Quanta-chip payment terminals
Reinforced inner-thigh panel on trousers—built for long standing/squatting shifts
Front kangaroo pocket on apron holding order-slip printouts and pen-stylus
Hi-vis silver strips on gilet shoulder seams—safety mandate for street workers
Bioluminescent flower sticker (personal, not corporate) glowing faintly blue inside cap brim—only soft, non-functional element in the entire outfit
Slightly scuffed black Foundry Broadfoot sneakers—authentic wear pattern from daily use
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 (Circuit working class). NutriRoute branding signals licensed vendor status—not corpo, not salvage. The outfit is standardized, functional, and visible by design. Investment in the gilet and proper footwear indicates stability and a legitimate route, not precarity.
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearing this outfit marks the wearer as Circuit infrastructure—a visible, essential worker in the GLMZ's food economy. NutriRoute vendors are ubiquitous at factory gates, transit hubs, and corridor intersections. The uniform says: 'I am licensed, I am reliable, I am here in all weather.' The bioluminescent flower sticker is a quiet rebellion—a personal touch in an otherwise corporate aesthetic, suggesting the vendor's individual humanity beneath the brand.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in but maintained. The pullover and apron are kept clean and stain-free (job requirement). The gilet shows patina at the shoulder seams and zipper pulls from repeated use. The cap brim is curved and worn low from daily sun/rain exposure. The sneakers are visibly scuffed at toes and heels—the wear pattern is authentic, not affected. Hands are bare and often chapped from cold or contact with food prep. The bioluminescent sticker glows softly, faintly—it's been there long enough that its glow has mellowed.

image_prompt: A Circuit-tier street vendor in full NutriRoute uniform stands at a rain-slicked transit hub at dusk. Safety orange pullover with white wordmark and QR sleeve patch visible under a charcoal quilted gilet; black reinforced trousers and oil-resistant Foundry sneakers ground the silhouette. A stain-resistant black apron covers the front, its kangaroo pocket visible. The NutriRoute mesh-back cap sits low, brim shadowing the face; inside the brim, a bioluminescent flower sticker glows soft blue—barely visible but present. Hands are bare and slightly chapped. The background is a modernist transit corridor with warm sodium lights casting long shadows; rain reflects on steel surfaces. Moody, utilitarian, authentic wear visible at seams and sole scuffs. The figure reads as essential infrastructure—reliable, visible, human beneath the corporate uniform. --ar 2:3 --v 6
